findings.statement: CA9 is up in tumors at both layers (RNA log2FC 6.312; protein log2FC 2.269, padj 9.9e-43, 84 pairs) with strong RNA-protein concordance (Spearman rho 0.797, padj 6.48e-24); convergence rank 1 (score 4.5279, 5 streams) with girentuximab in Phase 3. Membrane enzyme and classic HIF-driven ccRCC marker.

CD70 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.464, padj 4.13e-35) and protein (log2FC 2.421, padj 1.94e-38, 84 pairs) with high RNA-protein correlation (rho 0.843, padj 4e-29); a cell-surface ligand with vorsetuzumab/vorsetuzumab mafodotin listed, a strong antibody/cell-therapy target candidate.

COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is the top up-regulated protein (log2FC 3.768, padj 5.99e-48, 84 pairs) and RNA log2FC 6.752; RNA-protein rho 0.634 (padj 6.08e-13). Hypoxia-linked mitochondrial component; convergence rank 12 with 5 streams.

FLT1 (VEGFR1) is up at RNA (log2FC 2.021) and protein (log2FC 1.409); convergence rank 2 (score 3.9864, 5 streams) with pazopanib approved, consistent with the VEGFR-axis therapy already used in ccRCC.
MET is up at RNA (log2FC 1.342) and protein (log2FC 1.101); convergence rank 3 (score 3.8304) with foretinib listed; CNV gain frequency 0.255 and loss 0.018 suggest partial copy-number contribution.
CXCR4 is up at RNA (log2FC 2.859) and protein (log2FC 1.157); convergence rank 4 (5 streams) with burixafor and mavorixafor listed; likely partly reflects tumor immune infiltration.
EGFR is up at RNA (log2FC 1.461) and protein (log2FC 1.062); convergence rank 8 (score 3.5702) with EGFR inhibitors listed; CNV gain frequency 0.255.
SCARB1 is up at RNA (log2FC 2.974) and protein (log2FC 1.837); convergence rank 9; lipid-uptake receptor consistent with the lipid-rich clear-cell phenotype, no drug listed in the ranking.
PLIN2 is up at RNA (log2FC 2.62) and protein (log2FC 2.667, padj 7.99e-44); lipid-droplet marker reflecting the clear-cell lipid-accumulation phenotype.
PFKP is up at RNA (log2FC 2.72) and protein (log2FC 2.863, padj 7.05e-45); glycolytic enzyme indicating the Warburg-type metabolic shift.
ALDOB is strongly down (RNA log2FC -7.028; protein log2FC -2.273); proximal tubule identity loss, a diagnostic tissue biomarker rather than a target (rank 10, 5 streams).
ACY1 is down (RNA log2FC -3.529; protein log2FC -2.305) and lies in a region with copy-number loss frequency 0.809, consistent with 3p loss driving loss of tubule function.
VHL on 3p shows copy-number loss in 0.791 of 110 tumors (gain 0.027), underlying HIF stabilization that drives CA9, NDUFA4L2 and CD70 up-regulation.
PBRM1 (3p) shows copy-number loss in 0.8 of 110 tumors (gain 0.027), the second major 3p driver event.
BAP1 (3p) shows copy-number loss in 0.809 of 110 tumors (gain 0.027), part of the same 3p arm loss.

caveats: CPTAC discovery cohort only (110 tumors; 75 matched normals for RNA, 84 for proteome); no external validation.
Tumor-vs-normal bulk tissue: immune-related genes (CXCR4, CD74, PTPRC, FCER1G) may reflect infiltration rather than tumor-cell expression.
CNV is arm-level/segment loss frequency; 3p genes share one event so are not independent evidence.
Several findings cite RNA and protein ids together as returned by convergence_ranking; layer per id was not individually re-queried.
